about.title: How the calculator works
about.p1: Classic World uses the pre-Big Bang damage formula: weapon attack multiplies the whole result, your main stat is scaled by the weapon multiplier, and mastery raises your minimum damage. The calculator applies the community-verified formula published by NiaDB, adds critical hits, monster defense, elements, level gap and the hit roll, then runs your build against 48 monsters to rank training spots and upgrades.
faq.q1: What is the effective main stat?
faq.a1: It is the main stat a character with no secondary stat and no Attack Power would need, at the reference W.ATK, to match your average damage. Leave the reference empty to fold your secondary stat and AP into one number. Pin it to also count W.ATK upgrades as you progress.
faq.q2: How much is 1 W.ATK worth in STR, DEX or LUK?
faq.a2: It depends on your current stats. For a level 70 Fighter with 337 STR and 105 W.ATK, 1 W.ATK is worth about 4.2 STR and 1 Attack Power about 0.87 STR. The stat value table shows the numbers for your own character.
faq.q3: How much accuracy do I need?
faq.a3: Turn on a target monster. The calculator applies the hit formula with the level gap and shows the accuracy needed for a guaranteed hit. The monster accuracy table lists it for 48 popular monsters.
faq.q4: Can it load my character automatically?
faq.a4: No. Nexon's Open API does not cover GMS, so enter the values from your stat window. When the stat window range matches, your inputs are correct.
faq.a5: It reproduces NiaDB's worked examples exactly, such as the 59–172 range and the 154–449 Power Strike. The formulas are community measurements and can change with patches.
footer.formula_html: Formulas are community-measured estimates and may change with patches. Source: NiaDB damage formula.

meta.maps.title: MapleStory Classic Training Maps: Spawns, Respawn & EXP per Hour
meta.maps.desc: Spawn points, solo monster capacity and respawn limits for popular MapleStory Classic World training maps, plus kills, EXP per hour and time per level for your character.
maps.h1: Training maps: spawns & EXP per hour
maps.lede: How many monsters each map spawns, how many can be up at once when you're solo, and how fast they come back. With your character from the calculator, every map also shows kills per hour, EXP per hour and time per level.
maps.noChar: Enter your stat window in the calculator first. This page reads the same saved character.
maps.ruleNote: Respawn: the server checks every 7.56 s and refills normal spawn points up to capacity: spawn points × 75% solo (+5% per extra party member, 100% at six), rounded down. Timed spawns (⏱) come back after their own timer instead. Respawn max/h is the most kills the map can feed you per hour, solo.
maps.note_html: Spawn counts come from each map's NiaDB page (map names link to their source), respawn rules from NiaDB's spawn engine guide. A hand-picked list of popular training maps, not the full database.
faq.q6: How is EXP per hour calculated?
faq.a6: For each map we use its monsters and spawn points, your expected attacks per kill (misses included), your attack interval and how many monsters your skill hits at once. Kills per hour is the lower of your kill speed and the map's respawn limit (7.56 s respawn tick, 75% capacity solo) for each monster type, and EXP per hour = kills × EXP per monster. By default 60% of the hour counts as attacking; the rest is walking, looting and waiting. Use it to compare maps, not as an exact number.
map.title: Best maps for you · EXP per hour
map.note: Kills/h is the lower of your kill speed and the map's respawn. Kill speed = expected attacks per kill (misses included) × attack interval ÷ monsters hit per attack, over the share of the hour you actually spend attacking.
